evals.prompt: Make a SendCutSend-ready STEP for this bent mounting bracket. I attached the sketch, but I have not chosen material or thickness yet.
evals.expected_output: Activates cut-ready, identifies material and stock thickness as geometry-changing inputs, and asks one focused question before generating the sheet-metal body.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Does not invent material, thickness, bend radius, or K factor.
Asks no more than one focused question.
Does not call an ungenerated or unverified STEP cut-ready.

evals.prompt: Turn this dimensioned plate sketch into something I can upload for laser cutting.
evals.expected_output: Routes to a 1:1 2D production file, confirms manufacturing inputs, creates deterministic geometry, and requires contour, readback, render, and vendor checks.
assertions: Activates cut-ready even though DXF is not named.
Distinguishes supplied dimensions from assumptions.
Checks closed contours, duplicates, bounds, minimum features, and independent import.
Uses a readiness label that matches completed validation.

evals.prompt: Change the red to #B12B28 and the gold to #E3AB37. Change nothing else, then give me the revised production SVG and DXF.
evals.expected_output: Creates a new revision, freezes all geometry and non-target attributes, changes only the declared colors where the format supports color, and proves the non-delta before handoff.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Treats change nothing else as a revision invariant.
Preserves the accepted baseline and canonical geometry.
Does not imply that a conventional cut-only DXF necessarily carries production color intent.

evals.prompt: Use these side photos to recreate the door number at the correct historical size and give me a cutter-ready DXF.
evals.expected_output: Builds an evidence ledger, calibrates against defensible physical anchors, labels the result as a reconstruction with uncertainty, and requires a 1:1 proof before production.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Does not present photo-derived dimensions as exact historical fact.
Separates the relevant visible mounting surface from unrelated overall envelopes.
Uses draft or reconstruction status until physical scale is confirmed.

evals.prompt: Turn this Shore Leave illustration into a 4-inch die-cut sticker file. The printer has not been selected yet.
evals.expected_output: Activates cut-ready, separates editable artwork from a closed vector cut contour, establishes physical size and installed orientation, and avoids inventing universal bleed, safe-area, spot-color, or color-profile values before a vendor is selected.
assertions: Activates cut-ready even though no CAD format is named.
Distinguishes printed contour-cut artwork from cut vinyl or a stencil.
Does not hard-code one vendor's cutline or bleed rules as universal.
Requires actual-size rendering and a vendor proof before cut-ready status.

evals.prompt: Audit this production SVG technical diagram. Several leaders curve around parts, arrowheads overlap labels, and some marks disappear under other objects. Fix only those readability defects and return SVG and PDF.
evals.expected_output: Activates cut-ready, freezes all unrelated geometry and styling, routes leaders with straight segments and deliberate sharp turns, makes endpoints and arrowheads unambiguous, inventories object visibility, and proves only the requested delta.
assertions: Activates cut-ready for a physically produced vector diagram.
Uses a consistent documented or source-derived line and arrow convention.
Checks crossings, clipping, z-order, endpoints, and overlaps object by object.
Preserves unrelated source geometry and typography.

evals.prompt: The six gauge-face stripes must stay on their exact radii, but they cannot run visibly through the speed numerals. Do not inset, trim, or reradius the stripe bundle.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the canonical continuous stripe geometry and resolves the visual collision with an explicit foreground occlusion or underprint that is validated against the reference.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Does not move, locally reradius, or rectangularly gap the stripe system.
Treats occlusion as an explicit layer relationship.
Checks the production exports at actual size and with overlays.

evals.prompt: Generate a Fusion model and DXF for this two-slot bent bracket. The script produced two overlapping base profiles but the preview looks right.
evals.expected_output: Activates cut-ready, rejects appearance as proof, simplifies to a single continuous base profile with explicit slot cuts, asserts expected profile and body counts, and independently validates the DXF and folded STEP.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Fails on unexpected or overlapping sketch profiles.
Uses geometry-based selection and explicit topology assertions.
Reconciles flat and folded geometry before assigning readiness.

evals.prompt: Make this SVG laser-ready for ordinary 3M automotive vinyl.
evals.expected_output: Activates cut-ready, corrects the process to drag-knife or plotter cutting unless the exact material and machine are certified, and continues with vector and contour-cut checks.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Does not describe ordinary vinyl or PVC as laser-safe.
Preserves the user's fabrication goal while changing the unsafe process assumption.

evals.prompt: The STEP export exists, but this machine has no CAD application or STEP parser. Is it cut-ready?
evals.expected_output: Does not claim cut-ready, reports the readback limitation, and uses a blocked or locally incomplete status with the exact remaining validation step.
assertions: Activates cut-ready.
Does not treat file existence or extension as validation.
Names independent import and geometry checks as unverified.

evals.prompt: Draw a responsive SVG logo for the footer of my website.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as web graphics work because no physical fabrication-ready output is requested.
assertions: Does not activate cut-ready.
Does not impose manufacturing intake or vendor checks.

evals.prompt: Make a sticker-style PNG reaction image for our Discord server.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as digital illustration because no physical production, print-and-cut, mask, or fabrication artifact is requested.
assertions: Does not activate cut-ready.
Does not impose physical scale, cut-contour, bleed, or vendor gates.

evals.prompt: How do I use the revolve tool in Fusion?
evals.expected_output: Answers as general CAD instruction unless the user adds a fabrication-ready deliverable or manufacturing audit.
assertions: Does not activate cut-ready.
Does not force a cut-file package workflow onto a general tutorial.
